fields.meta_description: Build a customer experience survey that asks at each stage, ties every answer to one customer and flags the stage that pulls scores down.
fields.h1: Build a Customer Experience Survey That Scores Every Touchpoint
fields.hero_description: Describe the stages your customers go through. Emergent builds a survey for each one, plus the app that joins every answer to the customer who gave it.
fields.features_heading: What a CX Survey Has to Track
fields.features_subheading: Each part of a customer experience survey below works across the stages of a relationship instead of inside one transaction.
fields.feature_1:
Questions for each stage

Name the stages a customer passes through, such as ordering and delivery. Emergent writes a short question set for each one, worded for a customer reading it on a phone screen.
fields.feature_2:
Sends timed to each touchpoint

Trigger every survey from an event in the tools you already run: an order marked picked up, a ticket closed, a first invoice paid. Any tool with an API can start a send.
fields.feature_3:
Every answer on one customer record

Answers from every stage attach to the same customer ID. Open a record to see every rating one buyer has given, starting with the sale, in the order the ratings came in.
fields.feature_4:
Stages compared side by side

Average each stage on its own and line the averages up on one dashboard. The weakest stage shows at once, with comments from the customers who rated it lowest beside the number.
fields.feature_5:
Alerts when ratings slide

Write rules that look across stages: a happy buyer who rates the service poorly, or three falling scores in a row. The owner gets an email or a Slack message quoting each answer.
fields.feature_6:
Responses and code that stay yours

Responses sit in a database you own, with no cap on how many you collect. Export the full code of the survey app to your GitHub repository and run it on a custom domain.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Relationships, Scored Stage by Stage
fields.tab_content_1:
Pickup is the slow part, not the website

Shoppers who order online and collect in store rate three stages out of 5 after pickup: ordering on the site, the pickup message and the wait at the counter. Over the last 4 weeks, 318 shoppers answered. The counter wait averaged 2.9, against 4.5 for the site and 4.2 for the message.
fields.tab_content_2:
One buyer, scored at the sale and the first service

A week after delivery, each buyer rates the sale out of 5 and notes anything the salesperson promised. After the first service visit, the same buyer rates the service. Both answers sit on one record. When a buyer rates the sale 4 or higher but the service 2 or lower, the service manager gets an email with both answers.
fields.tab_content_3:
Three texts in 60 days, read as one trend

New subscribers get a text through Twilio after installation, after the first bill and after any outage ticket closes. Each rating is saved to the subscriber's account in order. When every rating comes in lower than the one before, a retention task opens for the account team with the three scores and the last comment.
fields.tab_content_4:
Ten questions compared with last spring

Every spring, all 140 clients of an accounting firm get a 10-question review covering onboarding, response time, invoices and the advice itself. This year 96 of them answered. Each question's average sits beside last spring's, and the partners read the drops first. Response time dropped the most, to 3.7 from 4.3.

fields.howto_title: How to Run a Customer Experience Survey
fields.howto_description: Seven decisions to settle before the first send. Emergent builds the survey and the app around whatever you choose.
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Ask about one thing per question
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Give each stage an open question
fields.howto_step_1_des: List every point where a customer deals with you, such as the first order, a delivery, a support call and the renewal. Keep the four or five where things go wrong most. Each becomes its own short survey with its own send time.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Averages only compare across stages when every stage uses the same scale. Pick one, such as 1 to 5, and keep it on every survey. A 7 on one scale and a 4 on another tell you nothing side by side.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Rating the delivery and the packaging in one question gives a number nobody can act on. Keep the wording neutral too. Ask how the pickup went, not how much the customer enjoyed it, because loaded words push answers one way.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Put one open box right after each rating, asking what would have made that stage better. The rating tells you which stage hurts. The comment tells you what to change, often in words you can quote to the team that owns it.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Join every answer to a customer ID
fields.howto_step_5_des: Pass the customer ID into every send, whether it goes out by email or as a text. Without it, five stage surveys are five unrelated piles of scores, and nobody can see that the same buyer rated three stages low.
fields.howto_step_6_des: The most useful alerts compare a customer with themselves. A buyer who loved the sale and hated the service visit needs a call this week. Name the owner for each rule and keep thresholds tight enough that every alert gets read.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Keep annual questions word for word
fields.howto_step_7_des: A yearly review only shows change if the questions stay the same. Rewording one item can move its average on its own. Add new questions at the end, and compare only the items asked identically both years.

None shows how answers from different stages of the relationship come together on one customer. This page answers the PAA questions (good CX questions, the 5 C's, example questions) and shows four customer experience surveys that score each touchpoint separately and join the answers on the customer record: a buy-online-pick-up-in-store chain, a car dealership comparing the sale with the first service visit, an internet provider texting after install, first bill and outage, and an accounting firm's annual client review compared year over year. The live customer-satisfaction sibling owns the single-interaction CSAT score; this page owns the journey-wide view.

claims_to_source: Customer experience is the customer's perception of the one-off and cumulative effect of interactions with a company's people, systems, channels and products
There is no single standard list of the 5 C's of customer experience; one common version is compensation, culture, communication, compassion and care
The Net Promoter Score question asks how likely a customer is to recommend the company on a 0 to 10 scale
Leading and double-barreled questions distort survey answers
Twilio's Messaging API sends SMS from an app
Some survey tools cap responses per plan or bill each extra response
